title: Forming the Jazz Prophets with Dick Katz and J. R. Monterose
summary: Dorham's band has Dick Katz, J. R. Monterose and Arthur Edgehill, and a weak rhythm section until Bobby Timmons is called.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So uh, so he got uh, Dick Katz, of all people, for the piano player. And there's a reason and uh, a saxophone player, another white boy from uh, man, he was
J. R. Montrose. Right. And uh, Arthur Edgehill, myself, that was the band.

That's right. So, and so we uh, then we went to--first gig was out in Cleveland somewhere. We played out there, man and never could get nothing going, man, you know, really, really get some rhythm section, man. Kenny said, 'man, there's a So uh, we heard about Bobby Timmons. So uh ... little dude over in Philadelphia, little old dude over there, I heard about some--everybody's talking about, about say I'm going to call him. Well I got his number.' So he -- sure enough we called him up. It was Bobby Timmons. And so we were working in the Cafe Bohemia .
And he called Bobby. Bobby came. And right away, man, rhythm section just took off.
